quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces crashes by preventing being "cut off."

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous and can lead to aggressive driving. You may receive a traffic citation for unsafe driving.

questions.question: If you had an argument and feel angry, you should:

options.text: Play loud music while driving so you don't think about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. If you are angry, upset, afraid, or worried, calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road, not on what upset you.

questions.question: When you see an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let aggressive drivers pass. Do not compete with other drivers. Follow traffic rules and respect other road users.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas in your vision when you get tired.
Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see using your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for blind spots. These are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: Nothing will likely happen.
You will be more alert.
You may not be able to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be able to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can make you unable to drive. They are even more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go slowly (15 mph) if you don't see children.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended stop arm. Stay stopped until the arm retracts and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the other direction.

questions.question: Vehicles must have liability insurance:

options.text: Only when driving on an interstate.
Only when a minor is driving.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: South Dakota law requires all vehicles to have insurance at all times. You must keep proof of insurance in your vehicle.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should only be driven:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
Under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under perfect conditions. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the limit. Safe speed is every driver's responsibility.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right to cross at crosswalks if they follow traffic signals. You must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A flagger is ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs and cones mark work zones. Stay alert for changes in driving conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is coming. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt system. Using only one part does not protect you well. Even if you have an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt too.

questions.question: What message appears on this yellow pennant-shaped sign?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, what should you do?

options.text: Still wear your seat belt.
You do not need to wear a seat belt.
Wear your seat belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For the best protection, use both your lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads make your tires grip less. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when you change lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when you change lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging in. Make space so drivers can safely join the flow of traffic.
Traffic is merging in. Stay to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging in. Make space so drivers can safely join the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you traffic will merge ahead. Check your side and rear mirrors. Move to another lane if you can to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where pedestrians can cross. Some crosswalks have additional lines between them. Crosswalks may also have no markings.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Wait for your body to process it.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process it.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects you quickly but leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. The only way to reduce it is to wait.

questions.question: How should a driver look while driving?

options.text: Stare straight ahead at the road.
Focus only on the center of the road.
Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light allows them to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near your vehicle at all times. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your car?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Create a habit before you start your car. Buckle your own safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and wave down the first car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the highway shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. High-speed traffic makes standing or walking on an interstate very dangerous.

questions.question: When must you obey school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools. You must always follow their directions.
